issues.body: reason_n3_query passes projected answers directly to a default ListExpander. ListExpander generates list cells named `_l1`, `_l2`, etc. without first collecting blank labels already present in those answers. A query can bind a conclusion variable to a data blank with one of those labels while also returning a list value; expansion then reuses the same blank for a list cell, merging two distinct RDF nodes and emitting a semantically wrong graph. The existing test only uses IRI/literal data and a constant list, so it cannot detect the collision.
issues.fix_hint: Before expanding query answers, reserve every blank label reachable in the rows (including nested list and quoted-triple members), and allocate list-cell labels from a fresh prefix/counter that cannot collide. Add an end-to-end reason_n3_query regression where the projected answer contains an existing `_l1`-style blank and a list, then assert the existing blank and generated list head remain distinct. Prefer making ListExpander collision-safe centrally so all callers inherit the fix.
issues.title: List expansion can merge generated cells with projected blank nodes

verdict.summary: The query path correctly reuses the native matcher and the focused builtin/list/formula tests exercise real evaluation. However, the new dictionary-returning API can silently corrupt list-valued answers because ListExpander allocates fixed `_lN` blank labels without reserving blank labels already present in projected answer terms. This is a wrong-answer bug on a newly public path and needs a collision regression test and namespace-safe allocation before approval.
